metadata.description: Editorial chronology scaffolding for the Millennial Week timeline: the 7 thousand-year 'days' (2 Peter 3:8), this site's creation epoch (with one comparison epoch), externally-anchored history, and prophetic milestones. Hand-authored from this repo's own studies -- not machine-generated like docs/data/genealogy/generated/*.json. The site works to ONE chronology line: the Masoretic numbers of Genesis 5 and 11 on a 1446 BC Exodus (creation 3959 BC). Every date here should agree with docs/content/last-things/chronology-anchors.md; the justifications are recorded in references/study-state/chronology-anchors.yml (decisions_2026-10-01) and genealogy-times.yml.

epochs.name: This site (Masoretic, Exodus 1446 BC)
epochs.note: Zadok year 0 = 3959 BC, counted as elapsed years since creation, so AM 3959 is AD 1 (there is no year zero). This is the epoch every published zadok_year uses: the a_prime scenario in docs/data/genealogy/index.json, active since 2026-10-01 (4004 BC, Ussher's 1491 BC Exodus, before that). Since 2026-08-22 the four genealogy variants in docs/data/genealogy/index.json each derive their OWN creation year from a shared Exodus anchor -- see each generated file's creation_bc -- so this value is the Masoretic variant's epoch, not a shared one.

epochs.name: dsscalendar.org epoch (comparison only)
epochs.note: Comparison only; this site does not date by it. dsscalendar.org's week boundaries put AM 6000 in AD 2075, which backs out to AM 0 = 3926 BC (it counts the creation year as AM 1, so its creation year is 3925 BC). The Day Is Near used it until 2026-10-01. About 34 years later than this site's epoch, and not derived from the Masoretic numbers or from 1 Kings 6:1, which is why the site follows the genealogical epoch instead. See feasts/zadok-calendar.md, 'Where year 0 sits'.

anchors.label: Jehoiachin's release (Evil-Merodach)
anchors.evidence: Jehoiachin's Ration Tablets (Weidner tablets), excavated Babylon

anchors.label: Merneptah Stele ("Israel" in Canaan)
anchors.evidence: Earliest extra-biblical mention of Israel as a people in Canaan -- a terminus ante quem for the conquest, not a date for the Exodus itself

anchors.label: Egypt's First Dynasty begins (accession of Aha, radiocarbon)
anchors.evidence: Dee et al., Proc. R. Soc. A 469 (2013) 20130395: 3111-3045 BC at 68% (3218-3035 BC at 95%), median 3085 BC. Before the Flood on the MT (2303 BC), SP (2893 BC) and Cainan-free LXX (2953-3053 BC) chronologies, all on the 1446 BC Exodus anchor; only Brenton's LXX with the second Cainan (3183 BC) precedes it. Radiocarbon estimate, not a synchronism -- a weaker anchor class than the others in this list.

anchors.label: Djoser's accession (Old Kingdom, radiocarbon)
anchors.evidence: Bronk Ramsey et al., Science 328 (2010) 1554-1557: 211 short-lived samples, Bayesian model, accession 2691-2625 BC (midpoint shown). About 355 years before the MT Flood date (2303 BC). Radiocarbon estimate, not a synchronism.

milestones.label: The Exodus (1 Kings 6:1)
milestones.note: 1 Kings 6:1's 480 years before Solomon's 4th year, counted back from Thiele's Qarqar-anchored 966 BC. This site's creation epoch is anchored here: AM 2513 on the Masoretic chain, so creation falls at 3959 BC. Not itself an anchor -- no independent record fixes the Exodus to a year, and a late-date Exodus in the 1200s BC is also held in scholarship.

milestones.label: Daniel's 69 weeks from 444 BC (Hoehner)
milestones.note: Harold Hoehner's count: 173,880 days from 1 Nisan 444 BC lands on 10 Nisan, 30 March AD 33 -- the reckoning this site follows. Sir Robert Anderson's earlier count from 445 BC reached AD 32, a year in which Nisan 14 does not fall on a Friday.

milestones.label: Year 6000
milestones.note: The close of Day 6 and threshold of the millennial Day 7, reading 2 Peter 3:8 with the creation week. AD 2042 on this site's chronology (creation 3959 BC), give or take the five years Solomon's fourth year carries. A chronological consequence, not a date for Christ's return: Jesus kept the day and hour hidden (Mark 13:32; Acts 1:7), and nothing in Scripture says the transitions are sharp.

milestones.label: Millennial reign begins
milestones.note: The start of Day 7 (Rev 20:2-7) -- Satan bound, the thousand-year reign begins.

anchor_table_note: Mirrors the table in docs/content/last-things/chronology-anchors.md row for row (number, date, tier, error bar, Zadok year). app/src/utils/chronology.test.js fails if the two disagree. 'core' rows show on the whole-week view; the rest appear when the view narrows.

anchor_table.label: Temple begun, Solomon's 4th year
anchor_table.evidence: 1 Kings 6:1's fourth year of Solomon, reached through Thiele's reconstruction of the regnal years from the Assyrian synchronisms. The Exodus 480 years earlier (1446 BC) anchors this site's creation epoch.

anchor_table.label: Shishak invades, Rehoboam's 5th year
anchor_table.evidence: Dated by 1 Kings 14:25 counted from Solomon's death in 931 BC; the identification of Shishak with Shoshenq I is widely held, and the Bubastite Portal at Karnak lists the campaign's towns without a date.

anchor_table.label: Ahab at Qarqar
anchor_table.evidence: Kurkh Monolith (Shalmaneser III), synchronized via the Assyrian Eponym Canon's Bur-Sagale eclipse (763 BC). Ahab is named as 'Ahab the Israelite'.

anchor_table.label: Jehu pays tribute to Shalmaneser III
anchor_table.evidence: Black Obelisk of Shalmaneser III, his 18th year: 'Jehu son of Omri' pays tribute.

anchor_table.label: Bur-Sagale eclipse
anchor_table.evidence: A solar eclipse in the Assyrian eponym list, computable to the day (15 June 763 BC). It turns the eponym list into an absolute chronology, and every Assyrian-Israelite synchronism inherits its precision.

anchor_table.label: Samaria falls, Hoshea's 9th year
anchor_table.evidence: 2 Kings 17:6 and the Babylonian Chronicle credit Shalmaneser V; Sargon II claims the capture in his own inscriptions.

anchor_table.label: Sennacherib besieges Jerusalem
anchor_table.evidence: Sennacherib's Prism (Taylor Prism) and the Lachish reliefs, British Museum. Sennacherib names Hezekiah.

anchor_table.label: Carchemish; Nebuchadnezzar accedes
anchor_table.evidence: Babylonian Chronicle BM 21946 (ABC 5): Nebuchadnezzar defeats Egypt at Carchemish and accedes the same year.

anchor_table.label: Jehoiachin deported
anchor_table.evidence: Babylonian Chronicle ABC 5 ("Jerusalem Chronicle"), BM 21946: captured 2 Adar, Nebuchadnezzar's 7th year (16 March 597 BC). 2 Kings 24:12 counts it as his 8th, Jeremiah 52:28 as his 7th.

anchor_table.label: Jerusalem falls; temple burned
anchor_table.evidence: 587 or 586 BC. No Babylonian chronicle survives for the year, so it is argued from biblical synchronisms; this site follows Thiele's 586.

anchor_table.label: Ezekiel's temple vision
anchor_table.evidence: Ezekiel 40:1, the 25th year of the exile, 'at the beginning of the year'. Whether that is 10 Nisan or 10 Tishri (the Day of Atonement) is contested.

anchor_table.label: Babylon falls to Cyrus
anchor_table.evidence: Nabonidus Chronicle: Babylon entered 16 Tishri (12 October) 539 BC.

anchor_table.label: Cyrus's decree
anchor_table.evidence: Cyrus Cylinder; fall of Babylon dated by the Nabonidus Chronicle (539 BC). Ezra 1:1, Cyrus's first year.

anchor_table.label: Work resumes, Darius's 2nd year
anchor_table.evidence: Haggai 1:1: 1 Elul in Darius's 2nd year, 29 August 520 BC.

anchor_table.label: Second temple completed
anchor_table.evidence: Ezra 6:15: 3 Adar in Darius's 6th year, March 515 BC.

anchor_table.label: Ezra returns, Artaxerxes' 7th year
anchor_table.evidence: Artaxerxes I's 7th year (Ezra 7:7-8). A minority places Ezra under Artaxerxes II (398 BC).

anchor_table.label: Decree to restore Jerusalem, 20th year
anchor_table.evidence: Elephantine papyri fix Artaxerxes I's regnal years independently. His 20th year is 445 BC on an accession-year count and 444 BC on the Tishri count that Nehemiah 1:1 (Chislev) and 2:1 (Nisan) in the same year imply; this site follows 444 (Hoehner), chosen to fit the AD 33 crucifixion -- see chronology-anchors.md entry 20.

anchor_table.label: Alexander breaks Persia at Gaugamela
anchor_table.evidence: Battle of Gaugamela, 1 October 331 BC. Daniel 8:20-21 names the ram as Media and Persia and the goat as Greece.

anchor_table.label: Alexander dies; the horn is broken
anchor_table.evidence: Alexander dies at Babylon in June 323 BC, aged 32: the great horn broken (Daniel 8:8).

anchor_table.label: Four kingdoms settled at Ipsus
anchor_table.evidence: Battle of Ipsus settles the four kingdoms of Alexander's successors (Daniel 8:22; 11:4).

anchor_table.label: Antiochus III takes Judea at Panium
Temple desecrated; the abomination set up
anchor_table.evidence: 1 Maccabees 1:54, 59: 15 and 25 Kislev in the 145th Seleucid year (December 167 BC).

anchor_table.label: Temple rededicated — Hanukkah
anchor_table.evidence: 1 Maccabees 4:52-54: 25 Kislev, 148th year (December 164 BC), 'at the very season and on the very day'. The Feast of Dedication of John 10:22.

anchor_table.label: Sabbatical year — siege of Beth-zur
anchor_table.evidence: 1 Maccabees 6:49, 53: Beth-zur surrenders for want of food in a sabbatical year.

anchor_table.label: Sabbatical year — Antiochus VII's siege
anchor_table.evidence: Josephus, Antiquities 13.234: the siege eased by a sabbatical year.

anchor_table.label: Pompey takes Jerusalem; Rome rules Judea
Sabbatical year — Herod takes Jerusalem
anchor_table.evidence: Josephus, Antiquities 14.475: Herod takes Jerusalem in a sabbatical year.

anchor_table.label: Nativity
anchor_table.evidence: Matthew 2:1 and 2:16 against Herod's death; Luke 3:23 pulls later. The bracket holds both.

anchor_table.label: Herod dies
anchor_table.evidence: Josephus's eclipse and Passover markers for Herod's death; 4 BC is the majority view, and a minority argues for 1 BC.

anchor_table.label: Temple "forty-six years" Passover
anchor_table.evidence: John 2:20's 'forty-six years', counted from Herod's start (20/19 BC) or from the sanctuary's completion (18/17 BC).

anchor_table.label: John's ministry begins
anchor_table.evidence: Luke 3:1-2: the fifteenth year of Tiberius, August AD 28 to August AD 29 counted from his accession in AD 14.

anchor_table.label: Crucifixion and Resurrection
anchor_table.evidence: Friday 3 April AD 33, this site's date. Only two Fridays in Pilate's prefecture carry Nisan 14 -- 7 April AD 30 and 3 April AD 33 -- and the year rests on Luke 3:1 read naturally, supported by Sejanus and by Daniel 9, which excludes AD 30 on either reckoning of the decree. AD 30 stays defensible if Tiberius's fifteenth year is counted from AD 13.

genesis_markers_note: Placed by Anno Mundi on the Masoretic chain, so their Gregorian year follows the epoch (creation 3959 BC). Derived from docs/data/genealogy/generated/mt.json and the Genesis intervals shown.

genesis_markers.label: Adam dies
genesis_markers.note: 930 years old, inside the first thousand-year day.

genesis_markers.label: Babel: the earth divided in Peleg's days
genesis_markers.note: Genesis gives only 'in his days'; Peleg lived AM 1757-1996. The population study models the dispersion about 200 years after the Flood.

genesis_markers.label: Abram born
genesis_markers.note: Terah 130 at Abram's birth, which Acts 7:4 requires on the Masoretic 205.

genesis_markers.label: Abram's call, leaving Haran
genesis_markers.note: Abram 75; the 430 years of Galatians 3:17 run from here to the Exodus.

genesis_markers.label: Jacob goes down to Egypt
genesis_markers.note: Jacob 130 (born AM 2168, Isaac 60, Genesis 25:26); 215 years before the Exodus.

future_sequence.note: UNDATED. Scripture gives the lengths (Daniel 9:27; Revelation 11-13; Daniel 12:11-12; Revelation 20) and withholds the start (Mark 13:32; Acts 1:7), so the axis counts years of 360 days from the covenant of Daniel 9:27 and carries no Gregorian or Anno Mundi date. The order follows this site's studies: The Rapture of the Church (the sequence diagram), Immediately After, Two Witnesses, The Trumpet Call of God and The Restrainer. certainty: 'stated' = the text gives it; 'site-reading' = this site's pretribulational, dispensational reading; 'contested' = where it falls is not stated and readings differ.

events.label: The rapture
events.note: Before the week begins, on this site's pretribulational reading. Scripture gives no interval between the rapture and the covenant, so its place on this axis is schematic.

events.label: The Bema: believers' works assessed
events.note: In heaven while the week runs on earth (the parallel track in The Rapture of the Church).

events.label: The marriage of the Lamb
events.note: Announced in Revelation 19:7-9, immediately before the rider on the white horse (19:11).

events.label: Covenant confirmed: the seventieth week begins
events.note: 'He shall make a strong covenant with many for one week' -- seven years of 360 days. This is day 0 of the axis.

events.label: Seals, trumpets and bowls
events.note: Revelation gives the order of the three cycles; where each falls within the seven years is not stated, and readings differ. Shown across the whole week for that reason.

events.label: The two witnesses, 1,260 days
events.note: 1,260 days, in either the first or the second half of the week. Scripture does not say which, and both are held.

events.label: Midpoint: the abomination of desolation
events.note: 'For half of the week he shall put an end to sacrifice and offering' (Daniel 9:27). Day 1,260.

events.label: Great tribulation: the beast's 42 months
events.note: 42 months = 1,260 days = 'a time, and times, and half a time', read as the second half of the week.

events.label: The second coming
events.note: 'Immediately after the tribulation of those days' (Matthew 24:29). The Church returns with Him (Revelation 19:14; Colossians 3:4). Armageddon and the beast's end follow (Revelation 16:16; 19:19-20).

events.label: 1,290 days from the abomination
events.note: Thirty days past the week's end. What the extra thirty days mark is not stated; readings include the cleansing of the temple and the judgment of the nations.

events.label: 1,335 days: "Blessed is he who waits"
events.note: Seventy-five days past the week's end; its content is not stated.

events.label: The millennium: Christ reigns, Satan bound
events.note: 'A thousand years', named six times in Revelation 20:2-7.

events.label: Satan released for a little while
events.note: After the thousand years; the length of 'a little while' is not given.

events.label: The Great White Throne
events.note: The dead judged by what they had done.

events.label: New heaven and new earth
events.note: God dwells with His people; the eternal state.

passion_sequence.note: AD 33 on this site's chronology: Friday 3 April (Julian) is Nisan 14, the crucifixion. Hours are counted from midnight at the start of Saturday 28 March; the Hebrew day runs from about 6 pm to 6 pm (Genesis 1:5; Leviticus 23:32), and clock times are the Gospels' hours (the third hour about 9 am). The three days and nights follow Three Days and Three Nights: three days touched, two nights, the third night being what the Friday reading has to absorb through inclusive reckoning (Matthew 27:63-64). Julian day labels are counted from 3 April; Hebrew dates assume a thirty-day Nisan and a twenty-nine-day Iyyar.

events.label: The Triumphal Entry
events.note: Monday 30 March, 10 Nisan, on Harold Hoehner's count of Daniel's sixty-nine weeks, which this site follows; 10 Nisan is the day the Passover lamb was chosen (Exodus 12:3). Tradition keeps Sunday 29 March. John 12:1, 12 puts it the day after Jesus reached Bethany 'six days before the Passover'.

events.label: The temple cleared
events.note: Mark places it on the day after the entry (11:12, 15). John records an earlier clearing at the first Passover of the ministry (John 2:13-22).

events.label: The Olivet Discourse
events.note: On the Mount of Olives, opposite the temple, in the last days before the Passover (Mark 13:3; 14:1). The exact day is not given.

events.label: "Two days before the Passover": the plot, and Judas
events.note: Mark 14:1 dates it two days before the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread.

events.label: The Last Supper
events.note: Thursday evening, as Nisan 14 began. The Synoptics call the meal the Passover (Mark 14:12); John has the priests still to eat theirs the next day (John 18:28). How the two relate is debated; Three Days and Three Nights places the meal at the start of Nisan 14, and the four-cups study reads it through the Seder's cups.

events.label: Gethsemane and the arrest
events.note: The same night, across the Kidron.

events.label: Trials: Annas, Caiaphas, the council, Pilate, Herod
events.note: Through the night; the council meets 'as soon as it was morning' (Mark 15:1). John 19:14 gives 'about the sixth hour' at Pilate's judgment, which is harmonised with Mark's third hour in more than one way.

events.label: Crucified: the third hour to the ninth
events.note: Crucified at the third hour, about 9 am (Mark 15:25); darkness from the sixth to the ninth hour (15:33); He dies at the ninth hour, about 3 pm (15:34-37). 'Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed' (1 Corinthians 5:7).

events.label: Burial before sunset
events.note: 'The day of Preparation, that is, the day before the Sabbath' (Mark 15:42), and the bodies not to remain on the cross on the Sabbath (John 19:31).

events.label: In the tomb
events.note: Guarded from the Sabbath (Matthew 27:62-66). 'After three days' and 'until the third day' are used by the chief priests a sentence apart (27:63-64): inclusive reckoning.

events.label: The women rest on the Sabbath
events.note: Having prepared spices, they rest 'according to the commandment'.

events.label: Spices bought, the Sabbath past
events.note: After sunset on Saturday, when the Sabbath was past.

events.label: The tomb found empty at dawn
events.note: 'Very early on the first day of the week, when the sun had risen' (Mark 16:2); 'while it was still dark' (John 20:1). The Gospels record the discovery, not the moment of rising.

events.label: Emmaus: "the third day since these things happened"
events.note: Luke 24:21, counted on the Sunday itself: Friday one, Saturday two, Sunday three.

events.label: He appears to the disciples
events.note: The evening of the first day of the week (John 20:19).

events.label: Forty days of appearances
events.note: 'Appearing to them during forty days and speaking about the kingdom of God' (Acts 1:3).

events.label: The Ascension, about the fortieth day
events.note: Thursday 14 May if the forty days are counted from the resurrection as day one. Acts gives 'during forty days', so the day is approximate.

events.label: The disciples wait in Jerusalem, praying
events.note: 'Wait for the promise of the Father' (Acts 1:4).

events.label: The Spirit poured out; Peter preaches; about 3,000 baptised
events.note: 'When the day of Pentecost arrived' (Acts 2:1), at the third hour of the day (2:15). Peter quotes Joel 2:28-32.

events.label: He washes the disciples' feet
events.note: 'Before the Feast of the Passover', during supper (John 13:1-2).

events.label: Bread and cup: "my blood of the covenant"
events.note: The cup 'after supper' (Luke 22:20) is where the Seder's third cup falls; see the four-cups study.

events.label: Judas goes out: "and it was night"
events.note: John marks the hour only as night (13:30).

events.label: A hymn, and out to the Mount of Olives
events.note: Across the Kidron valley to the garden.

events.label: Gethsemane: "not what I will, but what you will"
events.note: 'Could you not watch one hour?' (Mark 14:37): the prayer is measured in hours.

events.label: The kiss, and the arrest
events.note: Judas comes with a crowd from the chief priests; the disciples flee.

events.label: Before Annas
events.note: Questioned first by Annas, father-in-law of Caiaphas.

events.label: Before Caiaphas: "I am"
events.note: False witnesses; the high priest's question and Jesus' answer from Daniel 7:13 and Psalm 110:1.

events.label: Peter's three denials; the rooster crows
events.note: In the courtyard through the night. 'Cockcrow' is the Roman watch before dawn (Mark 13:35).

events.label: The council at daybreak
events.note: 'As soon as it was morning' (Mark 15:1); 'when day came' (Luke 22:66).

events.label: Before Pilate: "Are you the King of the Jews?"
events.note: 'It was early' (John 18:28). The accusers stay outside the praetorium so as to eat the Passover.

events.label: Sent to Herod Antipas, and back
events.note: Herod was in Jerusalem for the feast.

events.label: Barabbas released; Jesus scourged and crowned with thorns
"Behold your King!": handed over to be crucified
events.note: John gives 'about the sixth hour' here (19:14), Mark the third hour for the crucifixion (15:25); the two are harmonised in more than one way, and the difference is noted rather than resolved.

events.label: Simon of Cyrene carries the cross
events.note: Out of the city to Golgotha.

events.label: Crucified at the third hour
events.note: 'It was the third hour when they crucified him' (Mark 15:25).

events.label: "Today you will be with me in paradise"
events.note: Where Jesus and the thief were that day is taken up in Three Days and Three Nights.

events.label: "Woman, behold, your son"
events.note: His mother given to the beloved disciple.

events.label: Darkness over the land
events.note: From the sixth hour to the ninth.

events.label: "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?"
events.note: At the ninth hour.

events.label: "It is finished"; "Father, into your hands"; He dies
events.note: About the ninth hour, the afternoon the Passover lambs were slain.

events.label: The temple curtain torn; the earthquake; the centurion
Legs broken; His side pierced
events.note: 'Not one of his bones will be broken' (John 19:36; Exodus 12:46), the Passover lamb's rule.

events.label: Joseph of Arimathea asks for the body
events.note: 'When evening had come, since it was the day of Preparation' (Mark 15:42).

events.label: Laid in the tomb; the stone rolled
events.note: Nicodemus brings myrrh and aloes; the women see where He is laid.

events.label: The women set out "while it was still dark"
events.note: Toward the dawn of the first day of the week.

events.label: Earthquake; the angel rolls back the stone
events.note: The guards become like dead men. The order of the morning's events is harmonised in more than one way.

events.label: "He is not here, for he has risen"
events.note: 'When the sun had risen' (Mark 16:2).

events.label: Peter and John run to the tomb
events.note: The linen cloths lying there.

events.label: Jesus appears to Mary Magdalene
events.note: 'I have seen the Lord.'

events.label: He meets the women: "Greetings"
The guards report; the bribe
"Stay with us, for it is toward evening"
events.note: Known in the breaking of the bread.

events.label: "The Lord has risen indeed, and has appeared to Simon!"

feasts.label: Passover lambs slain (Nisan 14)
feasts.note: 'Between the two evenings' of Nisan 14 (Exodus 12:6): the afternoon Jesus died.

feasts.label: Unleavened Bread (Nisan 15-21)
feasts.note: Seven days; the first is a holy convocation. That Sabbath was 'a high day' (John 19:31).

feasts.label: Sabbath, first day of Unleavened Bread: "a high day"
feasts.note: The weekly Sabbath and the first day of the feast fall together in AD 33.

feasts.label: Firstfruits: the sheaf waved (Nisan 16)
feasts.note: 'On the day after the Sabbath the priest shall wave it' (Leviticus 23:11). Which Sabbath was disputed in the Second Temple period: the first day of Unleavened Bread, putting the sheaf on Nisan 16, or the weekly Sabbath, putting it on the Sunday. In AD 33 the first day of Unleavened Bread was itself the weekly Sabbath, so both readings give Sunday 5 April, the morning the tomb was found empty.

feasts.label: The counting of the omer: fifty days
feasts.note: 'Seven full weeks... fifty days to the day after the seventh Sabbath.'

feasts.label: Feast of Weeks (Pentecost), 6 Sivan
feasts.note: The fiftieth day from Firstfruits: Sunday 24 May AD 33. The Hebrew date assumes a thirty-day Nisan and a twenty-nine-day Iyyar.

three_days.label: Day 1 (part)
three_days.note: Crucified, dead at about the ninth hour, buried before sunset.

three_days.label: Night 2
three_days.note: In the tomb; the Sabbath past.

passion_sequence.three_days_note: Three days touched, two nights. The night of the Preparation is the one He was alive for. The Friday reading takes Matthew 12:40 by inclusive reckoning, the convention Matthew 27:63-64 shows in use; a Wednesday reading gives three nights and has to absorb Mark 15:42 and Luke 24:21. This site holds Friday.
passion_sequence.detail_note: Events marked detail show in the hour-by-hour views. timing 'stated' means the Gospels give the hour; 'approx' means the order is given and the hour is placed within it. Events marked summary stand for a run of detail events and show only in the wider views.
